Two students are investigating thermal energy transfer.
They are using the apparatus shown in Fig. 5.1.
iron block
beaker A
beaker B
Beaker A contains hot water and beaker B contains cold water at room temperature.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Record the temperature θH of the hot water and the temperature θC of the cold water as
shown on the thermometers in Fig. 5.1.
θH =  ...............................................................

content.html: Record the temperature θ<sub>H</sub> of the hot water and the temperature θ<sub>C</sub> of the cold water as shown on the thermometers in Fig. 5.1.
content.text: Record the temperature θH of the hot water and the temperature θC of the cold water as shown on the thermometers in Fig. 5.1.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Using metal tongs, one of the students places the iron block in the hot water in beaker A for
30 seconds.
He then removes the block and places it in the cold water in beaker B.
The other student then measures the temperature of the water in beaker B and finds that it
has risen to 35 °C. Their teacher suggests that this value is lower than expected.

matching improvement, e.g.
•

•
transfer more quickly
•
use insulated tongs/cotton round block

content.html: The students suggest that, immediately before the iron block was put into the cold water, the temperature of the iron block was not the same as θ<sub>H</sub>.
content.text: The students suggest that, immediately before the iron block was put into the cold water, the temperature of the iron block was not the same as θH.

content.html: Suggest one reason for this and a possible improvement to the experiment which could make the temperature of the block nearer to θ<sub>H</sub>.
content.text: Suggest one reason for this and a possible improvement to the experiment which could make the temperature of the block nearer to θH.

mark_scheme.label: 5(b)(ii)
mark_scheme.text:
•
some (thermal) energy transferred to beaker,
•
some (thermal) energy transferred to surroundings,
•
evaporation/convection (into atmosphere)
matching improvement, e.g.
•
use a less conducting material for beaker/owtte
•
insulate beaker
•
allow for beaker in any calculation
•
lid on beaker

content.html: The students also think that, when the block cooled in the water, not all of the thermal energy lost by the block raised the temperature of the water.
